- When sentiment shows strong positive spikes followed by sharp declines, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment volatility is high and news volume is constant, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overestimates continuation — apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature peak.
- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over 3+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–3% buffer to forecast for downward bias.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is rising, model often misreads sentiment — reduce forecast slope by 15–20% for negative sentiment trends.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate upward momentum in early weeks — cap forecast growth rate to 1.5x recent 7-day average.
